articleTitle: Enhancing Engineering Education: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Personalizing Learning and Outcomes
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Big Data Engineering and Education (BDEE)
abstract: The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) in educational contexts presents transformative potential for higher engineering education. This paper conducts a comprehensive literature review to explore the role of AI-driven analytics such as personalized learning pathways and adaptive assessment techniques, in personalizing learning experiences and improving educational outcomes for engineering students. Through a systematic analysis of existing research, we identify how AI technologies - such as machine learning algorithms, data mining, and natural language processing - can be utilized to tailor educational content, improve learning engagement, and optimize curriculum design. A synthesis of the findings highlights the significant benefits of AI in identifying diverse learning styles, predicting academic performance, and providing real-time feedback, thus fostering a more individualized and effective learning environment. In addition, this article discusses the challenges and ethical considerations associated with implementing AI in education, including data privacy, algorithmic bias, and the need for human oversight to ensure ethical AI deployment. Building upon insights gleaned from a thorough review of published literature, we propose a conceptual framework for integrating AI into engineering education, with the aim of equipping the students with the skills and knowledge required to navigate the complexity of the modern engineering landscape. This theoretical exploration underscores the transformative potential of AI in engineering education and sets a foundation for future empirical research to further investigate and expand upon these benefits and strategies.

articleTitle: A Survey of Vision-based Fire Detection using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Big Data Engineering and Education (BDEE)
abstract: Fire can harm humans and animals and destroy the natural environment. Early and accurate fire detection is crucial. However, detecting fire is very challenging due to its varying color, size, shape, texture, and the uncertainty of different environments. In this paper, we review literature on datasets, attention mechanisms, and networks, which are the most important components of a fire detection model. We first present key notations to describe the network structure and its key components. Then, we introduce several attention mechanisms to reduce the false alarm rate. After that, we present numerous state-of-the-art neural networks for fire, flame, and smoke detection. Finally, we discuss several challenges and opportunities at the end of this paper.

articleTitle: Research on University Teaching Evaluation Information System Based on Multi-Users
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Big Data Engineering and Education (BDEE)
abstract: Based on the teaching evaluation system of universities, this paper deeply analyzes the teaching evaluation indicators and processes, and proposes a multi-user college teaching evaluation information system. The system is aimed at students, teachers, supervisors, leaders and teaching evaluation office staff. Functional modules including student evaluation, teacher mutual evaluation, supervisor evaluation, and leader evaluation have been developed, which can comprehensively and multi-angled reflect the teaching process of teachers, thereby promoting college teachers to improve the teaching quality.

articleTitle: Application and Development of Digital Twins in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Big Data Engineering and Education (BDEE)
abstract: This paper synthesizes existing research to explore the synergistic relationship between the advancement of digital twin technology and the evolving landscape of smart cities. It delves into the mechanisms by which digital twins are integrated into smart city frameworks, positioning digital twins as pivotal components in the evolution of these urban environments. Understanding the influence of digital twin technology on smart cities is crucial for fostering the deployment of digital technologies in future urban settings. Moving forward, the seamless integration and application of 5G, cloud computing, the Internet of Things (IoT), blockchain, artificial intelligence, digital twins, and 3R technologies (virtual reality, augmented reality, mixed reality) will be essential for the development and management of smart cities. The investigation into the utilization of digital twin technology within smart cities aims to enhance the efficiency of resource allocation and urban governance.

articleTitle: Design and Practice Exploration Method of Teaching Mode Based on Big Data
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Big Data Engineering and Education (BDEE)
abstract: With the rapid development of Internet of Things technology, IoT development platforms provide students with broad learning and practical space. However, how to effectively evaluate the learning effectiveness of students on IoT development platforms has become an urgent issue in the field of education. This article proposes a Outcome Based Education (OBE) model, which utilizes an IoT development platform to enhance student learning abilities. It collects and analyzes student learning behavior data on the IoT development platform, constructs a learning evaluation model, and achieves precise evaluation and personalized guidance of student learning outcomes. Practical cases have shown that this teaching model can effectively improve the learning effectiveness and motivation of students, making a positive contribution to the improvement of teaching quality in universities.

articleTitle: IEFDNet: Detection of Fire Using Partial Convolution Inception
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Big Data Engineering and Education (BDEE)
abstract: Vision-based fire detection approaches using deep convolutional neural networks have achieved significant improvement. However, how to make a good tradeoff between model accuracy, size, and inference speed is still challenging. EFDNet is the state-of-the-art fire detection network; however, its lower inference speed limits its deployment on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we first analyze and visualize the channel output shape, parameters, and floating-point operations (FLOPs) of every layer in EFDNet to investigate what truly limits the inference. We uncover that the main reason causing the high FLOPs issues in EFDNet is the branch containing a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\times 5$</tex> convolution in the third inception module. To address this issue, PConvInception is proposed, which introduces partial convolution to replace the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\times 5$</tex> convolution. The experimental results conducted on the FD dataset show that our proposed method achieves an accuracy of 95.18%, comparable to that of EFDNet, while having 8% higher inference throughput on GPU, as well as saving 63% compute time on CPU.

articleTitle: The Application and Challenges of Artificial Intelligence in Supporting Educational Innovation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Big Data Engineering and Education (BDEE)
abstract: Amid the rapid development of information technology, artificial intelligence (AI) has brought profound changes to the field of education. By analyzing AI applications in China's educational innovation, this paper explores the potential and challenges of AI in educational reform and proposes strategies to promote the scientific, intelligent, and personalized development of the education system. Specific applications demonstrate AI's practical effects in enhancing teaching efficiency, enriching learning experiences, and improving intelligent education management. This study provides theoretical support and practical guidance for the comprehensive upgrading and optimization of the education system, summarizes the challenges of AI education technology and looks forward to the future development trend.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Optimization of Insurance Sales Strategies: Challenges and Opportunities in China's Aging Society
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Big Data Engineering and Education (BDEE)
abstract: This paper presents an in-depth analysis of the applications of artificial intelligence in optimizing insurance sales strategies within the Chinese market. It explores the practical implementations of deep learning, natural language processing, and other technologies in domains such as sales forecasting and customer engagement. Additionally, it investigates the specific challenges arising from an aging population and the complexity of financial insurance products. The study further discusses potential future research directions for the insurance industry, focusing on leveraging artificial intelligence to enhance sales strategies considering an aging demographic. China is on the verge of having the world's largest aging population, and the findings of this research can serve as a reference for other regions globally.

articleTitle: SINe: Out-of-Distribution Detection by Selecting Important Neurons
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Big Data Engineering and Education (BDEE)
abstract: Detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) samples is an essential task when deploying machine learning models in open-world scenarios. Quantifying the uncertainty of input samples is of great importance, particularly in mission-critical domains like autonomous driving and medical diagnosis. In these fields, accurate predictions are crucial, as failures on OOD detection can cause significant problems. Modern neural networks are powerful prediction models for in-distribution (ID) samples, but they are prone to producing highly confident predictions on OOD data, leading to misclassification. In recent years, numerous methods have been proposed to address this issue, with post-hoc OOD detection methods being extensively explored because they do not require an additional retraining process that might degrade the model's performance and increase the training cost. We propose a new method called Selecting Important Neurons (SINe) for post-hoc OOD detection. Our method focuses on the neurons in the deep layer of the model that represent the high-level features. Our key idea is to use Shapley value-based pruning to reduce the effects of noise signals by selecting neurons that meet the following criteria: first, the selected neurons should make significant contributions to predicing specific classes of in-distribution samples; simultaneously, the selected neurons are not significant for OOD samples. We empirically demonstrate that SINe achieves competitive detection performance on a comprehensive suite of benchmark datasets, and provide theoretical explanation for our methods efficacy.

articleTitle: Image Perception and Promotion of Chuancais Museum Based on Online Big Data
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Big Data Engineering and Education (BDEE)
abstract: Chuancais Museum plays an important role in the dissemination of Sichuan cuisine culture. Building a good tourism image is crucial for the long-term development of tourist destinations. In this paper, the tourism evaluation related to Chuancais Museum is analyzed, which is mainly done by crawling the data related to visitors' comments from the major UGC website through Octoparse information collector. ROSTCM6 software is used to gain the perceived image of tourists to the museum. The image perception is studied from three aspects: cognitive image, emotional image, and overall image. The research results indicate a positive trend of the overall image for Chuancais Museum with a relatively positive overall evaluation. In response to the negative evaluation from tourists, the author mainly puts forward suggestions from four aspects: evaluation channels, transportation routes, ticket purchasing models, marketing and promotion, hoping to contribute to the continuous improvement of the tourism image of Chuancais Museum.

articleTitle: A Review of Machine Learning Methods to Solve Flight Scheduling Research
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Big Data Engineering and Education (BDEE)
abstract: The crew scheduling problem is a crucial component of airline operations planning. Using traditional operations research optimization methods to optimize the crew scheduling process can enhance the scientific and accurate nature of the plan, significantly impacting the airline's operational efficiency, cost savings, and ensuring the safety of flight operations. However, due to the increasing number and complexity of modern flight schedules, traditional combinatorial optimization algorithms face enormous computational pressure and cost. Additionally, the need for timely recovery of problem flights imposes limitations on traditional methods. Therefore, by reviewing recent algorithms that use machine learning to address combinatorial optimization problems, this research explores and examines the integration methods, algorithmic logic, and areas for improvement. It also investigates the potential of these methods for solving flight scheduling issues, providing insights and references for future applications of machine learning in addressing flight scheduling problems.

articleTitle: Large Language Models Enhanced Client Simulation and Feedback System for Insurance Advisors
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Big Data Engineering and Education (BDEE)
abstract: Traditionally, training insurance advisors to improve their sales skills has been challenging. This has often involved static methods such as script memorization and workshops, which lack personalization and fail to adequately replicate real-world client interactions. To address this issue, we developed an innovative training system that utilizes large language models (LLMs) to create intelligent agents that simulate difficult client interactions and provide evaluative feedback. Our system comprises three agents: two that simulate difficult client scenarios in telephone and face-to-face settings, and one that functions as an evaluator, providing feedback and suggestions for improvement. We collected and annotated over 1,000 real sales interaction recordings to train these agents, creating a comprehensive dataset. The system was tested with 50 insurance advisors, resulting in significant improvements in sales success rates, client satisfaction scores, advisor confidence levels, and response times compared to traditional training methods. This study underscores the effectiveness of LLMs in providing personalized, realistic, and immediate training experiences, highlighting their potential to revolutionize training methodologies in the insurance industry.

articleTitle: Applying Data Science in Computer Vision: Detection of Malignant and Benign Cancer Tumors
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Big Data Engineering and Education (BDEE)
abstract: Tumors are abnormal growths of tissue that can either be malignant or benign. Malignant tumors indicate cancer, while benign tumors are generally minimally harmful. The difference between the two is not evidence at first glance, and many tests must be conducted to identify it. Tumors need to be determined at an early stage, considering that treatments are most effective during the early stages of cancer when it has still not yet infected a lot of cells. Computer Vision is a technology that enables computers to simulate the “perceiving the real world” phenomena. With it, computers can create analyses and conclusions based on different images provided. With computer vision, a good data set is essential. Data Science makes use of different preprocessing techniques that aid in analyzing data. Applying different preprocessing methods to a data set allows the creation of high-quality data that can be used as a training data set for computer vision models. There are various computer vision models; the models that will be discussed are CapsNet, VGG16, ResNet50, and GoogLeNet. Concurrently, their accuracy and performance would be compared to each other. Furthermore, the importance of data science relative to computer vision will also be discussed. The increase in accuracy of having preprocessed high-quality data as a data set for computer vision models will also be measured.

articleTitle: Digitalization Empowers Cross-border Education in the Post-pandemic Era on the Basis of China-Africa Cultural Memory Project
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Big Data Engineering and Education (BDEE)
abstract: The arrival of the post pandemic era on a global scale has driven digital technology to play an increasingly important role in promoting cross-border education in universities. This paper will first expound on the inevitability of digital transformation as a trend for cross-border education. It will then explore specific instances where digital technology enhances transnational education by examining a project titled “Cultural-memory Community between China and Africa on the Maritime Silk Road” supported by questionnaire surveys. Research has shown that with the use of digital education, the comprehensive level of teaching and learning has been improved, the students' 5C language skills have improved, and the students' intercultural culture acquisition and critical thinking skills have shown a positive trend. Furthermore, the paper will offer recommendations from both hard and soft power levels to facilitate digital transformation in cross-border education during the post-pandemic period.

articleTitle: Research on Teaching Reform of Spark Big Data Analysis Course Based on TOPCARES-OBE
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Big Data Engineering and Education (BDEE)
abstract: Focusing on the issues of students' low efficiency in learning real-time big data processing and analysis techniques, as well as their weakness in solving comprehensive real-time big data problems, this article, guided by the TOPCARES teaching method and based on the OBE and student-centered educational philosophy, takes the Spark Big Data Analysis course as an example to reform theoretical teaching methods and practical teaching modes. In theoretical teaching, we adopt an outcome-oriented online and offline hybrid teaching method. In practical teaching, we use a teaching mode that combines OBE-CDIO-based classroom and extracurricular smart cloud platform project practice. This can not only consolidate students' theoretical foundation of Spark big data but also improve their ability to solve comprehensive big data problems. Finally, we study the evaluation mechanism of course goal achievement and calculate the degree of course goal achievement. By comparing the average values of course goal achievement between the 20201–20204 big data classes and the 19201–19204 big data classes, it is found that the average achievement rates of course goal 1, goal 2, and goal 3 of the 20201–20204 classes are 3%, 4%, and 2% higher than those of the 19201–19204 classes respectively. Meanwhile, a questionnaire survey was conducted among students, and the average satisfaction rate of students with the course was 92.55, indicating that the teaching reform has achieved certain results and can provide references for other similar curriculum reforms.
